reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address V substitution in HfMoTaTiZr, density reduction, or the specific mechanical property targets. E1 discusses strengthening mechanisms in other alloys, and E2 compares Hf-containing RHEAs but provides no data on V effects, density, or the claimed property retention. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: V is significantly lighter than Hf, so partial substitution reduces density by 10–15%.
V has similar electronic character to Hf, preserving lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening.
Limited V substitution causes minimal lattice parameter change, maintaining a single-phase BCC structure.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has ~1600 MPa RT yield strength and ~855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Maintaining single-phase BCC ensures RT and high-temperature yield strengths stay within ±5% of baseline.
